title: pvGradientMagnitude
body:
## pvGradientMagnitude

Computes the magnitude of the spatial gradient of an image's point scalars with central differences that account for the pixel spacing, giving image data of the same size (edge values use one-sided neighbours). It is the classic edge-strength image, useful to locate interfaces or fronts. Dimensionality decides whether the z derivative is included. For gradients of general meshes, or vector results, use gradient.

Common mistakes and assumptions:

- The output has the input's scalar type, so an integer image gives a truncated integer magnitude; convert to float first when precision matters.
- Multi-component scalars are differentiated per component, not combined.
- Schemaxis generates this binding from ParaView's catalogue; it has not run a native acceptance check for this operation.

Native constructor: `GradientMagnitude`. Identity: `filters/GradientMagnitude`. Role: `pipeline`. Output kinds: `["data"]`.

ParaView: This property specifies the input to the Gradient Magnitude filter. Accepted data: image data (uniform rectilinear grids) (vtkImageData). The input needs at least one point-centred array with 1 component. | True | one object | `data` | `{"compatibility":"native-domain-checked","composite":null,"cost":{"basis":"no benchmark","conversion":"none inserted","rating":"unknown"},"nativeTypes":["vtkImageData"],"requirements":{},"traits":{"contiguity":"unknown","indexing":"unknown","iteration":"unknown"}}` |

If computing the gradient magnitude in 2D, the gradients in X and Y are used for computing the gradient magnitude. | `{"type":"enum","values":["Two","Three"]}` | `native initialisation / omitted` | `"Two"` |
